record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Is every smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type rigid?

evidence.quote:
RIGIDITY CONJECTURE (H. Flenner-M. Zaidenberg [FlZa]). Any smooth
Q-acyclic surface X of log-general type is rigid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field of complex numbers. A smooth complex algebraic surface $X$ is called $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic if its rational (singular) homology groups satisfy $H_i(X;\mathbb{Q})=0$ for all $i\ge 1$, i.e. $X$ has the rational homology of a point. Choose a smooth projective compactification $\overline{X}$ of $X$ such that the boundary $D=\overline{X}\setminus X$ is a simple normal crossing divisor; then $X$ is said to be of log-general type if the logarithmic Kodaira dimension $\overline{\kappa}(X)=\kappa(\overline{X},K_{\overline{X}}+D)$ equals $2$. The pair $(\overline{X},D)$ is called rigid if it admits no non-trivial equisingular (locally trivial) deformations; equivalently, $H^1(\overline{X},T_{\overline{X}}(-\log D))=0$, where $T_{\overline{X}}(-\log D)$ is the logarithmic tangent sheaf.

Prove or disprove: every smooth $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic complex algebraic surface $X$ of log-general type is rigid in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The Flenner–Zaidenberg rigidity conjecture for $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic surfaces of log-general type appears to remain open. Recent work (e.g., Koras–Palka and collaborators on rational cuspidal curves, ca. 2013–2024) treats the conjecture as an unproven assumption and verifies special cases (such as planar rational cuspidal curves of low degree), and a "weak rigidity" version is studied in connection with the Coolidge–Nagata conjecture, but no full proof or disproof was located.

status_evidence.title: Classification of planar rational cuspidal curves I
status_evidence.snippet: The Flenner–Zaidenberg Weak Rigidity Conjecture ... is equivalent to the vanishing of h^0(2K_X+D) and implies the Coolidge–Nagata conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The Flenner–Zaidenberg rigidity conjecture is treated as an unresolved conjecture used to derive other results.

status_evidence.title: On the Number of the Cusps of Rational Cuspidal Plane Curves (Piontkowski)
status_evidence.snippet: Flenner and Zaidenberg conjectured that (D, V) is always rigid and unobstructed.
status_evidence.claim: The original Flenner–Zaidenberg rigidity statement is referenced as an open conjecture.
